Study 03

Edge detection criteria upgrade

2026-08-19 · fibrecv · branch worktree-edge-criteria

Low-confidence fibers 6 → 1
Per-part RMS (p50 / max) 3.70→2.78 · 11.8→6.3
Synthetic delta 3.90 → −0.51 px
Bright-mode knobs frac 0.30 · k 6.0

Introduction

Study 02 (multi-angle cross-section) found that 6 of 15 C1 fibers were flagged low-confidence due to large per-angle ellipse residuals. Investigation identified two causes in the edge detection pipeline:

  1. Z-map choice: max(R,G,B) rides the outermost chromatic aberration fringe, adding a systematic 1–4 px wide bias on all bright-mode images.
  2. Fixed threshold: edge_z=4 sits at roughly 5–10% of band amplitude on C1 images (amplitude 40–70 z), deep in the defocus halo skirt. Defocus pushes the detected edge 15–25 px outward.

Study 01 (erf-midpoint) had shown that a 50% midpoint causes “inward bite” on cylindrical fibers. Any relative threshold must therefore be clamped below 50%. This study replaces the z-map with median RGB and introduces a clamped two-sided threshold formula.

Method

Two changes were made on the worktree-edge-criteria branch, both gated to feature_mode == "bright" (the desat path for MasP2 is completely unchanged):

1. Z-map: max → median. In features.py, the bright-mode intensity channel was changed from rgb.max(axis=2) to np.median(rgb, axis=2). The median of 3 channels equals the middle value, rejecting the single channel where chromatic aberration concentrates.

2. Threshold: clamped relative. In edges.py, the threshold formula for bright mode became:

level = base_val + max(edge_z, min(edge_frac * A_side, edge_cap * A_side))

Where edge_z=4.0 is the absolute floor, edge_frac is the primary relative knob, and edge_cap=0.50 prevents convergence on the study-01 failure point.

Calibration. edge_frac was swept over [0.15, 0.20, 0.25, 0.30, 0.35, 0.40, 0.45] with edge_cap=0.50, measuring two criteria:

  • Criterion 1 — Synthetic circle per-side edge bias δ: must stay in [−1, +4] px.
  • Criterion 2 — Real C1 30-image sample: width stability (std, IQR) and low-confidence count.

3. Coupled recalibration of k_band. A first full run exposed a coupling the z-map change created. k_band=4.0 is an absolute z threshold for the coarse band mask, calibrated against the max(R,G,B) z-scale. The median z-map has a smaller background MAD, so z-scores inflate and more of the defocus halo crosses 4.0. On the six most defocused C1 images the coarse band ballooned (band_half 97.5→159.0, 89.0→141.5, 97.5→222.5 px) while the measured widths stayed correct, collapsing band_ratio = width / band_thickness to 0.326–0.483 — below band_ratio_min=0.5 — and raising a false band_mismatch that excluded those images from stage 3.

The consequence was worse than the flag. The six angles are 60°-spaced (0/60/120/180/240/300), which modulo 180° form three direction pairs. Fiber 01 part 4 lost a2/a3/a5, leaving a1/a4/a6 — directions 0°/0°/120°, only two distinct directions, rank-deficient for a three-parameter ellipse. That part produced zero valid fits from 3495 columns, and fiber 01's low_confidence flipped True→False because the rms gate only saw the surviving parts.

k_band was therefore swept over [4, 5, 6, 7, 8] on the six problem images plus eleven controls. False mismatches fall to zero at k≥5; the problem-set band_ratio minimum rises 0.326→0.646 (k=5)→0.705 (k=6)→0.761 (k=7); and measured widths are identical at every k (144.2 px problem, 147.6 px control), confirming k_band moves only the coarse mask, never the boundary. On the twelve hardest/dimmest images coverage slightly improves (min 0.732→0.753 at k=6) with widths drifting 0.1%. k_band=6.0 was selected, giving 0.205 headroom above the gate. All results below are from the re-run with this fix.

All six formerly low-confidence fibers cleared; 13 of 15 improved. Fiber 08 showed the largest rms improvement (11.84 → 4.64 px, −61%). Median part_rms_med_max_px fell 4.97 → 4.10 px. Across all 75 parts the residual distribution tightened substantially: p50 3.70 → 2.78, p90 6.64 → 4.39, max 11.84 → 6.27, and parts above 6.0 px fell from 11 to 1. Total measured positions are essentially preserved (162 223 → 161 634, −0.4%), confirming the improvement is not an artifact of discarded data.

Fiber 10 is the one regression, and it is not a threshold artifact. Because the six angles form three direction pairs, rms_resid_px is purely pair disagreement. In part 1 the pair medians |Δ| moved a1−a4 1.91→6.76, a2−a5 2.73→20.44, a3−a6 7.14→5.01. The a2/a5 pair locked roughly 500 px off during cross-angle x-registration (rms 20.37 at lag 0 versus 4.92 at lag +508; an independent raw-profile search puts the true lag near +710), and part 3 shows the same failure on a3/a6 at +512. Per-image coverage is normal on all 30 images (0.97–1.00 valid-column ratio versus the old run), so edge extraction is not at fault. The cause is that the ~10.6% global width shrink altered the cross-correlation landscape enough to flip the peak choice. This is a stage-3 registration robustness issue, outside the scope of the edge criteria, and is recorded as a follow-up.

Synthetic circle control

Per-side edge bias δ on a rendered 190 px circle (6 projection angles, noise σ=0.03):

  • Old pipeline (max z-map, edge_z=4 fixed): δ = 3.90 px/side
  • New pipeline (median z-map, edge_frac=0.30): δ = −0.51 px/side

The bias dropped from a consistent 4 px wide overshoot to near-zero, within the [−1, +4] acceptance band.

Visual spot-check

Discussion

The hypothesis is confirmed: replacing max(R,G,B) with median(R,G,B) and switching to a clamped relative threshold substantially reduces defocus-induced width errors on C1 bright-mode images without introducing inward bite.

The median z-map was the dominant improvement. The chromatic fringe that max rides is a single-channel artifact — the median ignores it by construction. This alone would have been sufficient to clear most of the formerly-bad fibers, as evidenced by the synthetic delta dropping from 3.90 to −0.51 px even at the legacy edge_frac=0.65.

The clamped threshold provides additional stability and principled calibration. The two-sided formula max(edge_z, min(edge_frac·A, edge_cap·A)) separates three concerns: an absolute floor for faint walls, a calibratable relative position on the wall, and an upper clamp that prevents the study-01 inward-bite failure mode. The calibration sweep showed clean monotonic trends with no boundary-value selection.

MasP2 is provably untouched. Three MasP2 images were run through both branches in desat mode: median diameters 80.52685546875, 62.23075866699219 and 42.61311340332031 µm with deltas of exactly 0.0. The full diameter_raw arrays and the float32 D z-maps match by SHA-256 on all three, so the change is bit-identical from the first pipeline stage onward, not merely at the output.

An absolute threshold coupled to a changed scale. The k_band defect is the instructive failure of this study. Changing the z-map changed the meaning of every absolute z threshold downstream, and k_band was the one that mattered. It was caught only because a part silently produced zero fits — the flag itself pointed at fiber 01 while the real damage was rank deficiency in the ellipse fit. Relative thresholds (edge_frac, edge_cap) are immune to this class of coupling by construction, which is a further argument for the relative formulation beyond the defocus stability it was introduced for.

Verdict. The hypothesis is confirmed. Median-RGB z-map plus a clamped relative threshold removes the systematic wide bias (δ 3.90 → −0.51 px/side, visually confirmed on sharp, defocused and dim images), clears all six formerly low-confidence fibers without discarding data, and tightens the per-part residual distribution throughout (p50 3.70 → 2.78 px, parts above 6.0 px 11 → 1). The MasP2 desat path is bit-identical. One regression remains — fiber 10 — and it is a genuine stage-3 registration lock failure, not an edge-detection defect or a threshold artifact.

Caveats and follow-ups

  • Fiber 10 registration lock. Cross-angle alignment picks a wrong correlation peak (~500 px off) on two parts. The width shrink changed the correlation landscape and exposed it; the underlying fragility is pre-existing. Fix belongs in stage-3 peak validation, not here.
  • Absolute thresholds under a changed z-scale. k_band was recalibrated; amin=3.0, rise_min=2.0, slope_min/slope_cap are also absolute in z and were not individually re-swept. They showed no symptoms across 450 images (coverage 99.7%, zero errors), but they carry the same coupling in principle.
  • xsec_rms_flag_px=6.0 was left unchanged though the distribution it was calibrated against has moved (p90 6.64 → 4.39). It now sits above p95 rather than near p90. Retaining it is deliberate — it still isolates exactly the one genuinely defective part — but it is stricter in relative terms than when calibrated.
  • Bright-mode defaults live in the CLI, not the dataclass. CONFIG defaults remain desat-calibrated; --feature-mode bright applies BRIGHT_DEFAULTS in run_measure.build_config. Callers that construct CONFIG(feature_mode="bright") directly (tests, any future GUI bright mode) do not get them and must set edge_frac and k_band themselves.
  • Axis ratios shifted (grand median 1.127 → 1.139). A uniform width shrink inflates the ratio geometrically, so part of this is expected artifact rather than a change in measured shape; the two contributions were not separated here. Study 02's anisotropy conclusions should be recomputed on the new run before being restated.
